cause.event: A new write request (S_AXI_AWVALID=1) arrives while the previous write response is pending (axi_bvalid=1, S_AXI_BREADY=0).
S_AXI_AWVALID, S_AXI_WVALID, and S_AXI_ARVALID are all asserted in the same clock cycle.
The last data word is ready to be transmitted, and the downstream slave stalls (M_AXIS_TREADY goes low).
On cycle 3, state_next is not combinationally updated to STATE_TRANSFER_OUT when input_axis_tvalid becomes high.
A write operation occurs when the FIFO is almost full, causing the write pointer to advance to a state that the faulty `full` logic misinterprets as not-full.
The first clock cycle after reset is de-asserted.

In FRAME_FIFO mode, when the FIFO is full (i.e., wr_ptr_cur_reg has caught up to rd_ptr_reg), the buggy `full` logic fails to assert, causing an extra write to be accepted and `wr_addr_reg` to be incremented, pointing to a memory location that should not be written to.
The `rst` signal is asserted while `drop_frame` is 1.
A new single-beat frame arrives (monitor_axis_tvalid & monitor_axis_tready & monitor_axis_tlast & !frame_reg).
A grant to a port other than the one with the highest index causes the round-robin mask to be updated to a value that incorrectly restricts subsequent grants, breaking the round-robin behavior.
When normalizing the result of a subtraction with leading zeros in the mantissa, e.g. `(-1.25) + 1.0`.
During startup hold, the logic to reload the SPI clock divider is unconditional, preventing the divider from counting down and asserting r_z_counter.
